r1.action: Verify source power, disconnect, breakers, and upstream electrical supply.

r2.action: Verify transformer primary and secondary voltage, low-voltage breaker, and wiring.

r3.action: Determine cause with safe electrical testing before resetting. Inspect for shorts and overloads.

r4.action: Test fuses, inspect hidden fuse holders and Panduit, then replace only after finding the cause.

r5.action: Confirm transformer VA loading, correct the overload, and reset if permitted.

r6.action: Record LED pattern, verify power quality, allow boot time, and follow controller recovery procedure.

r7.action: Continue with EBO status, application, bindings, and communications checks.

r8.diagnosis: Automation Server cannot be reached locally
r8.action: Verify USB cable/driver and controller boot state; escalate for recovery or replacement if needed.

q101.question: Is the UI16 status light normal?

q104.question: With field wires removed, does jumpering the input change the UI state?

q105.question: With field wires removed, does opening/closing the input change the UI state as expected?

q106.question: At the field device, does simulating the contact change the controller state?

q107.question: Is the 4-20 mA transmitter two-wire or three/four-wire?

q115.question: Is expected signal voltage measured at the controller terminals?

q116.question: Does the voltage also fluctuate on the meter?

q117.question: Does measured voltage correspond to the expected engineering value?

q118.question: When applying a known-good signal, does the input respond correctly?

q119.question: Is expected voltage present at the field device output?

q120.question: Does the displayed value match the field measurement and configured scale?

q121.question: At the sensor, is resistance open/OL?

q122.question: At the sensor, is resistance near 0 ohms?

r101.diagnosis: UI16 module connection or module-health issue
r101.action: Check S-cable/module connections, module power, status LEDs, and controller I/O bus status.

r102.action: Verify the input object, physical channel, signal type, and test with a known-good input/channel.

r104.diagnosis: Controller and wiring respond to contact simulation
r104.action: Investigate the field contact/device, its power, setup, and mechanical operation.

r105.action: Tone and identify conductors; verify terminations at the correct field device and panel input.

r106.action: Restore correct DC loop power after checking breakers, fuses, polarity, and supply rating.

r107.action: Verify the separate power source and correct voltage type before continuing.

r109.diagnosis: Signal is present in field but absent/different at controller
r109.action: Check continuity, polarity, shorts, grounds, and terminations between device and controller.

r113.diagnosis: Incorrect or missing device supply voltage
r113.action: Correct device power source, polarity, and nominal voltage.

r114.diagnosis: Field transmitter calibration or scaling mismatch
r114.action: Compare output signal to process condition; verify transmitter range and calibrate or replace.

r115.diagnosis: Unstable signal originates at field device
r115.action: Verify device stability, power quality, grounding, shielding, and nearby electrical noise.

r116.diagnosis: Controller scaling, filtering, or point setup issue
r116.action: Verify input type, engineering range, units, filtering, and conversion.

r117.diagnosis: Measured signal does not match expected process value
r117.action: Verify transmitter configuration, sensing tubing/mechanics, calibration, and signal wiring.

r118.diagnosis: Controller input operates with a known-good signal
r118.action: Investigate the field device, its calibration, power, and wiring.

r119.diagnosis: Field device is not generating the expected signal
r119.action: Verify device power, setup, process connection, and operation; repair or replace.

r120.diagnosis: Input and displayed value appear normal
r120.action: Investigate sequence logic, bindings, graphics, trends, and system operation.

r121.action: Isolate sensor from wiring; repair open conductors/terminations or replace sensor.

r122.action: Isolate sensor from wiring; locate the short or replace the sensor.

r123.diagnosis: 10k Type II sensor is out of tolerance
r123.action: Confirm with chart and calibrated reference; replace the sensor if required.

r125.action: Configure the EBO input as 10k Type II and verify the reading.

r126.action: Continue with application logic, setpoints, operating mode, and equipment operation.

r127.action: Correct mounting, seal wall penetrations, improve thermal contact, or relocate the sensor.

r202.diagnosis: DO relay/contact is not switching correctly
r202.action: Verify wet/dry contact requirements and common wiring; test a known-good output, then repair/replace module.

r203.diagnosis: DO8 module or application is not responding
r203.action: Verify module status, I/O bus, application download, channel object, and controller health.

r204.action: Continue downstream to starter, relay, contactor, VFD, motor, or mechanical equipment.

q304.question: Does measured output voltage match the commanded percentage and configured scale?

q306.question: Does the actuator or VFD respond across the command range?

q320.question: Is the output command changing as expected in EBO?

q321.question: Can current be measured safely in series at the output?

q322.question: Does measured current match the commanded percentage and configured scale?

q323.question: Does the same current reach the field device and cause a response?

r301.diagnosis: 0-10 V output does not match command
r301.action: Verify AO signal type, scale, common/reference, loading, point configuration, and module channel.

r302.action: Investigate actuator setup, VFD parameters, linkage, sequence, or mechanical equipment.

r303.action: Verify module health, current-output configuration, loop wiring, and correct meter connection.

r304.diagnosis: 4-20 mA output does not match command
r304.action: Verify range, loop load, polarity, channel configuration, and test with a known-good device.

r501.action: Restore correct power and resolve abnormal LED/startup condition before network troubleshooting.

r502.action: Verify USB connection and boot state; perform approved recovery or replace hardware if required.

r503.action: Check switch power/ports, cabling, VLAN, routing, firewall, and upstream network equipment.

r504.action: Verify server association, certificates/time if applicable, controller name/address, and EBO communication settings.

r505.action: Correct IP, subnet, gateway, DNS/server association, and duplicate-address conditions.

r520.action: Check trunk power, master controller port, polarity, topology, termination, shorts, and baud rate.

r521.action: Assign a unique MAC address and recommission the device.

r522.action: Set compatible baud rate and Max Master values across the trunk.

r523.action: Correct polarity, daisy-chain topology, shield grounding, end-of-line termination, shorts, and stubs.

r524.diagnosis: A downstream segment or device is disrupting the trunk
r524.action: Reconnect in sections to isolate the cable/device, then repair wiring or replace the failing transceiver.

r525.diagnosis: Individual device communication hardware or setup issue
r525.action: Verify device power, address, firmware, port configuration, then replace if it fails independently.

r540.action: Verify physical link, switch port, cable, VLAN, subnet, gateway, duplicate IP, and device network settings.

r541.action: Correct addressing/VLAN and coordinate network changes before recommissioning.

r542.diagnosis: BACnet service/configuration issue on local subnet
r542.action: Verify BACnet/IP enabled state, UDP port, device instance, and local firewall.

r543.action: Investigate bindings, object references, server discovery cache, and application configuration.

r544.action: Review packet captures/logs and server/device discovery settings for intermittent or application-level issues.

r545.diagnosis: BBMD, foreign-device, routing, or firewall issue
r545.action: Correct BDT/FDT entries, broadcast distribution, UDP port rules, and routing.

r560.action: Check VFD grounding, shield practices, cable separation, and induced noise on communications/power.

r561.action: Measure voltage during events, verify transformer loading, grounding, and power-supply health.

r562.diagnosis: Intermittent network issue not yet isolated
r562.action: Review event logs and trends; inspect connectors, switch errors, trunk statistics, and environmental conditions.

r563.diagnosis: Single device or segment is intermittent
r563.action: Inspect local power, terminals, transceiver, cable segment, address, and device logs.

r580.diagnosis: Field value is incorrect at the controller
r580.action: Route to the applicable temperature, AI, or DI input workflow.

r581.diagnosis: Communication values match end to end
r581.action: Investigate sequence logic, graphics presentation, alarms, units, and operator expectations.

q810.question: Is space/supply-air temperature accurate and is cooling enabled?

q820.question: Is temperature accurate and is heating enabled?

r801.action: Identify smoke, freeze, pressure switch, overload, condensate, proof, or manufacturer lockout; correct cause before reset.

q903.question: Are safeties/interlocks and lead-lag selection normal?

r903.action: Investigate display/logic expectations or intermittent mechanical operation.

r1002.diagnosis: BMS enable reaches boiler but boiler does not fire

r1302.action: Investigate belts, rotation, dampers, duct restrictions, motor/VFD setup, and mechanical condition.
